mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 anticipates future rate hikes, causing a negative 20-day forward return as discounting future cash flows at higher rates reduces expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following the trigger, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from a 0% return (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increases are <0.25% in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) coincides with rising consumer confidence, which accelerates corporate hiring and boosts S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-trigger, SPX 60d returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS spike (Spearman's rho < 0.2), or hiring decelerates within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDPC1 (goods orders) and HOUST (housing starts) rise simultaneously by at least 5% in a quarter, it indicates robust demand across sectors, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up >=5% AND HOUST up >=5% in the same quarter
failure_condition: In 20 days following the dual-proxy uptick, SPX 20d returns are negative or flat, and at least one of GDPC1 or HOUST reverses direction within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% suggests supply-side weakness, which typically precedes a 5-day S&P 500 bearish trend when combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 252).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls 3% in a month AND CPIAUCSL < 252
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive days post-trigger, SPX shows no sustained downward trend (max drawdown < 1%), or CPIAUCSL rises above 252 within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: During a 3-month period where FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5%, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as markets anticipate continued easing.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%, SPX 20d returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rises above 1.5% within the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% triggers a labor-market tightening that precedes a 60-day S&P 500 bearish trend as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-UNRATE drop below 4%, SPX 60d returns show no significant negative mean (p > 0.05), or UNRATE recovers within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When both RSAFS (retail sales) and PAYEMS (new job growth) exceed their 12-month averages by at least 8%, it signals a momentum shift toward growth, producing a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS up >8% YoY AND PAYEMS up >8% YoY in the same month
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the double-proxy surge, SPX 20d returns are flat or negative, or either RSAFS or PAYEMS reverts below their 12-month averages within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in GDPC1 (goods orders) of over 8% in a quarter, without a corresponding rise in HOUST (housing), predicts a 60-day S&P 500 decline as it reflects demand-side weakness without housing recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 down >8% in a quarter AND HOUST flat or down in the same quarter
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-GDPC1 contraction, SPX 60d returns show no significant negative trend (p > 0.05), or HOUST rises by >5% within the period.
